slot_rules.source: hyperreal cockpit (2026-11-15, scene 12): the cabin slots -- c172p-interior.ac and the 26 instrument faces (beauty_only parts of assets/aircraft_config/c172p.json), plus the glareshield, panel board, seat mounts and glovebox that c172-common.ac draws on the same panel / panel_parts / interior textures -- fell to default_class paint: the livery's clear coat (1.0, coat roughness 0.08), panel-line grooves at 60/50/30 cm, wear, grime and soot on the gauge faces, which read dark and flat. Every number is a slot-level look choice applied on top of the paint class (scripts/aircraft_look.py slot rule scalars): no clear coat (a printed dial, a crackle-painted board, vinyl and carpet have none), no grooves, no wear, no grime, no soot, no roughness breakup; Roughness 0.61 is roughness_from_shininess(12), the pinned .ac materials' shi 12 on every instrument (mag-compass.ac MATERIAL lines) -- the same formula fg_material would apply. The slot names are the converter's mat_<texture stem> (assets_pipeline/convert.py material_key) for every texture the interior parts reference at a15d83d1; an exterior texture (fuselage, wing, tail, glass-alpha) does not match.
